skill.name: alembic
skill.description: Database migration management for SQLAlchemy projects using Alembic.
skill.summary: Manage SQLAlchemy database schema changes with Alembic workflows and examples.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The shell execution alerts are Markdown code fences and Alembic examples, not hidden Ruby backtick execution. Database URL examples are legitimate for migrations but handle credential-bearing connection strings, and one destructive downgrade example lacks explicit safeguards.

remediation.issue: Database connection strings appear in migration configuration examples.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholders and add guidance to load secrets from approved secret stores without logging or committing them.

remediation.issue: The downgrade-to-base example can remove an entire schema.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to require backups, staging validation, and explicit approval before destructive downgrade commands.

remediation.issue: Command examples can affect live databases if copied without context.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend checking the active database target and running migrations in staging before production use.

content.value_statement: SQLAlchemy teams need reliable schema changes without losing migration history. This skill guides Alembic setup, revision creation, upgrades, downgrades, branching, and migration checks.
actual_capabilities: Shows commands for generating, checking, upgrading, downgrading, and inspecting Alembic revisions.
Provides async SQLAlchemy env.py configuration using target metadata and async engines.
Demonstrates manual migration operations for columns, tables, indexes, constraints, and batch mode.
Explains filters for schemas, temporary tables, and custom autogenerate behavior.
Includes snippets for database revision checks and programmatic migration execution.
Covers branch migrations, merge revisions, and common dependency setup.
limitations: Does not inspect your live database or verify generated migration safety.
Examples must be adapted to your project settings, models, and database driver.
Downgrade and destructive operations require careful review before execution.
Does not replace backups, staging tests, or production change approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare SQLAlchemy Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Generate and review Alembic migrations for model changes before applying them to a shared database.

use_cases.title: Standardize Migration Workflow
use_cases.description: Document repeatable commands and review steps for teams using Alembic across services.

use_cases.title: Validate Deployment Readiness
use_cases.description: Check current revisions, pending heads, and branch merges before a database release.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Migration Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Alembic change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a safe Alembic workflow for a SQLAlchemy model change. Include generation, review, upgrade, and rollback planning steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Generated Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before applying a migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Alembic migration for unsafe operations, missing downgrade steps, data backfill needs, and staging checks.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Async Alembic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for async SQLAlchemy projects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through configuring Alembic for async SQLAlchemy with target metadata, database URL handling, and autogenerate options.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Branching Release Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release planning with multiple migration heads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a migration release with multiple Alembic branches, merge revisions, deployment order, validation checks, and rollback constraints.

output_examples.input: I need to add a required full name column safely.
output_examples.output: A staged migration plan with a nullable column, data backfill, not-null change, and a review checklist.

output_examples.input: Our migration branches diverged before release.
output_examples.output: A branch strategy that identifies current heads, creates a merge revision, and verifies upgrade order before deployment.

output_examples.input: We use async SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL.
output_examples.output: An environment setup outline that maps project settings, target metadata, async engine configuration, and Alembic checks.

best_practices: Review autogenerated migrations before applying them to any shared database.
Run migrations against a staging copy before production deployment.
Keep downgrade logic explicit unless your team has approved one-way migrations.
anti_patterns: Running downgrade base against a shared or production database without approval.
Storing database URLs directly in tracked Alembic configuration files.
Accepting empty or destructive autogenerated migrations without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and manage Alembic migrations for SQLAlchemy projects, including setup, revisions, upgrades, downgrades, and branch merges.

faq.question: Can it generate a migration for my exact project?
faq.answer: It can guide the workflow and review expected steps, but your local tools must generate migrations from your project models.

faq.question: Does it support async SQLAlchemy?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async env.py patterns using async engines, target metadata, and Alembic configuration.

faq.question: Is it safe to run downgrade commands?
faq.answer: Downgrades can be destructive. Review the migration, confirm the target database, and keep backups before running them.

faq.question: Can it help with multiple migration heads?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes branch labels, targeted upgrades, and merge revisions for divergent migration histories.

faq.question: Does it manage database credentials?
faq.answer: No. It shows where connection strings fit, but secret storage and access controls remain your responsibility.
